entry.label: Canon formation
entry.description: The social and editorial processes through which some people, works and traditions become the recognised centre of a field while others become marginal, derivative, invisible or difficult to retrieve.
entry.canonical_definition: The social and editorial processes through which some people, works and traditions become the recognised centre of a field while others become marginal, derivative, invisible or difficult to retrieve.

profile.summary: Canon formation is the production of a recognised centre and periphery in a field through selection, teaching, citation, institutional power and repetition.
profile.canonical_definition: Canon formation is the production of a recognised centre and periphery in a field through selection, teaching, citation, institutional power and repetition.
profile.why_it_matters: The atlas cannot criticise other maps for false neutrality while leaving its own visibility choices implicit.
common_misreadings: A canon is not simply a list of the objectively best people.
Replacing one closed list with another does not remove boundary choices.
open_checks: Add explicit cases of exclusion, appropriation, canonisation and recovery only where public evidence supports the precise relation.
